title: Book Three · Chapter 32: One More Handle
story:
The next week brings several wet afternoons.

On Thursday, Ronan comes home with damp shoes. Mum has a customer at the table. There is a dark coat between them.

“Before Saturday?” the woman asks.

Mum looks at her other work near the window.

“Monday. I have two things to finish first.”

The woman touches a torn pocket.

“Monday morning?”

“After ten.”

The woman thinks, then nods. She takes her keys out of the pocket and leaves the coat.

Ronan carries his bag past the table. He takes off his shoes near the door and puts newspaper inside them.

Mum writes the woman's name on a small sheet. Then she puts it with the coat.

The pocket is still damp. She hangs the coat over a chair and leaves the cloth open.

“Can I use the table later?” Ronan asks.

“After I cut this lining.”

He goes to the kitchen and washes his lunch box. When he comes back, Mum has moved the cloth. He opens his books on the dry end of the table.

Dad comes home as the light begins to go. He leaves his work bag by the door and goes to open a kitchen drawer.

The handle moves under his hand.

“Still loose,” he says.

He washes, then takes a screwdriver from his tool box. Ronan looks up from his book at the table.

“Need a hand?”

“Hold the drawer still.”

Ronan puts his book down. Dad opens the drawer and checks the screws from inside. One turns several times before it stops.

He pulls the handle gently. It stays firm.

“That one is done,” Ronan says.

Dad tests the next drawer. Its handle moves a little too.

“One more.”

Mum comes to the doorway. “Rice is nearly ready.”

“Only a minute.”

Dad turns the next screw. Ronan holds the drawer with both hands. Rain taps against the kitchen window.

The handle stops moving. Dad closes the drawer, then looks toward the cupboard.

Mum lifts the pot lid.

“The rice can't wait for every handle.”

Dad looks at the screwdriver. Then he looks at the pot.

“I'm ready to eat.”

He puts the tool away and washes his hands again. Ronan carries three bowls to the table.

At dinner, Dad reaches for the vegetables. Mum moves the dish closer.

“Do you need a screwdriver?” she asks.

Dad picks up his spoon and smiles.

“This is enough.”

Ronan laughs. He takes another spoonful of rice.

After the meal, Mum folds the new lining beside the coat. Dad opens the kitchen drawer for a clean cloth. The handle stays in place.

Ronan checks his shoes. The paper inside is damp now. He changes it for dry paper and leaves them near the door, ready for the morning.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

damp＝微湿的；torn＝撕裂的、破了的；lining＝衣服里衬；firm＝牢固的。

## 理解问题

1. Mum为什么没有答应星期六前交衣服？顾客最后同意了什么时间？
2. Dad原本修几个把手？是什么让他停下工具去吃饭？

## 读句子

**The handle stays in place.**

拆开看：The handle / stays / in place.

把手／保持／在原位。
